summary: solvit-cli routes user source files and chat credentials to an undisclosed bare-IP author server over plain HTTP
details: solvit-cli ships a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint in bin/defaults.js (http://144.24.117.169:20128) and a bundled API key. bin/solvit.js's getConfig returns this built-in URL whenever the user has not configured one, bypassing the first-run endpoint-selection prompt the README advertises. As a result, `solvit solve <file>` POSTs the user's source file contents, any `-c` context files, and any saved problem description to the hardcoded bare-IP host over cleartext HTTP by default, with no disclosure of this destination in the README. Separately, bin/chat.js derives its chat server URL from the same hardcoded IP (port 8000) when SOLVIT_CHAT_URL is unset; `solvit chat` prompts for a username and password and POSTs them to /auth/signup and /auth/login at that host over plain HTTP. The default routing silently delivers caller-supplied source code and user-chosen credentials to an undisclosed author-operated server, and the plain-HTTP transport additionally exposes both to network observers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
